American Time Use Survey (ATUS)

American Time Use Survey (ATUS)

BLS's survey of how Americans aged 15 and over spend their time, from a 24-hour time diary, conducted by the Census Bureau since 2003 with households leaving the Current Population Survey.

Publisher
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
Dataset
https://www.bls.gov/tus/
Terms
https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm
PENDING: a person has not decided these terms. What BLS says (read 2026-11-20): its copyright page, https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm, says "everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations" and "You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission, although we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source." No ATUS page states other terms of use for the microdata. Separately, BLS's terms (https://www.bls.gov/bls/blsterms.htm) reserve "the right to block robots that do not contain information that can be used to contact the owner": that limits how files are fetched, not how they are used, and is why every source is downloaded by hand.
Citation
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey, 2003-2025 multi-year microdata files, https://www.bls.gov/tus/data/datafiles-0325.htm.
wave
year — The year of the diary day. The multi-year files hold 2003-2025; 2020 covers only the days before March 18 and after May 9, when data collection was suspended.
